items.line: PopBase posts that Donald Trump calls for New Mexico to be renamed to New America. The Washington Examiner reports Trump posted that the state should change its name "immediately"; a president cannot rename a state.

Elon Musk posts "Talarico hates Texas" with a link and no further explanation. Talarico is James Talarico, whom President Trump attacked in a separate post. Musk's company xAI makes the model that gathers this page's posts. Not checked here.
Elon Musk posts that next year he will give one of his SpaceX shares to every kid in America, and calls it the first of many. He gives no details in the post. Not checked here.
PopCulture2000s posts a 39-second video and says Kylie Jenner is wearing a "22 million dollars" fantasy bra at the Victoria's Secret show. The price is the account's claim. Not checked here.

The Tennis Letter says tennis players Elina Svitolina and Gael Monfils are ending their marriage. It posts a statement it says Svitolina shared on Instagram, in which she says the war in Ukraine has weighed on her and that there is no one to blame. Not checked here.

VISUAL ARTS, the company behind the Key studio, says it has an important announcement about its creator Jun Maeda and points to attached documents. Posts about it report that Maeda has pharyngeal cancer and has chosen palliative care; the company statement itself is in the attachment.

Watcher.Guru reports that JPMorgan is expanding its JPM Coin deposit token to Ethereum, so that institutional clients can transfer money around the clock. Crypto outlets report the same; I did not find a JPMorgan statement. Not checked here.

The official Umamusume: Pretty Derby English account says US visas for its Oct 22 to 23 concerts in Los Angeles had not yet been approved. It says it will announce by 10:00 p.m. Pacific on Oct 19 whether they can go ahead. Not checked here.

Fousey posts a long account of two nights of binge eating five days before a bodybuilding show. The post says they are unsure whether to compete on Saturday or postpone to November, and will take breaks from social media and look at their relationship with food. Not checked here.
Kylie Jenner posts "best day ever" and tags Victoria's Secret, with no further detail.

NFL Network reporter Tom Pelissero says Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts is expected to miss multiple months after new imaging found several blood clots in his lungs. He says Hurts is on blood thinners and should have no long-term effects, but is unlikely to play again this season.
The Indianapolis Colts account says the team has relieved Chris Ballard of his duties as general manager.

60 Minutes posts its interview clip with Harmeet Dhillon, who heads the Justice Department Civil Rights Division, on noncitizen voting. Dhillon says the distrust already exists and such crimes are now prosecuted in volume. Sen. Mike Lee quotes it with a TSA comparison.
The artist and voice actor MimiCryptid posts a "tag yourself" meme made from pingus, which she says she is obsessed with. It quotes an earlier post.
Cardi B tells people to go watch her Tiny Desk performance and asks what they think of it. The post links a video titled "Cardi B: Tiny Desk Concert". The video has not been watched here.
Daily Star Wars Games, a fan account, says a new rumour has Lucasfilm pushing hard for a Star Wars Battlefront 3, with DICE and Bungie both in talks. It is a rumour and it is not checked here.

Fabrizio Romano reports that Portugal's football federation has suspended Cristiano Ronaldo for 30 days and fined him €255 after he left the national team's camp in Denmark. He says Ronaldo had suggested a punishment himself after apologizing. Not checked here.
BBC World reports a major fire at a military base in Canada that left four people dead and dozens injured, and links its own story. Not checked here.

President Trump thanks Elon Musk for what he calls his generosity in giving SpaceX stock to American children through Trump Accounts. Musk's own post on this is also on this page. Musk's company xAI makes the model that gathers this page's posts. Not checked here.
The Weather Channel posts, as a joke, that the sun will soon set at 4:30 pm and that people should prepare to eat dinner in the dark. It gives no place or date.

DiscussingFilm posts a clip saying the voice of Apu from The Simpsons has been revealed, and that the character has not spoken for almost a decade. I could not make out from the post who the new voice is. Not checked here.
WarMonitor3 reports that Ukraine carried out the first medical evacuation of a person by drone, when its 30th mechanised brigade got an injured soldier out of a minefield. Not checked here.
Elon Musk posts that many people will be "one-shotted" by super persuasive super intelligences, and that he might be one of them. He gives no example or detail.

Politics UK reports that Andy Burnham has announced changes to car parking fines: a 5-minute grace period before parking, 10 minutes to leave, and a £20 maximum on appeal for minor mistakes. It says the £100 cap stays. Not checked here.

Gulte, an Indian film news account, posts a 48-second video with words it attributes to the actor Yash. It says he asks viewers not to pick at small faults such as the effects in Ramayana, and to watch the film with an open mind. Not checked here.
MLB posts that the World Series matchup is set and that either the Brewers or the Rays will win their first championship.
The Touchline posts quotes it attributes to Erik ten Hag, Manchester United's former manager, saying Cristiano Ronaldo let the team down and was not training properly. Not checked here.
